Resource_Provisioner.message: PROVISIONER STANDBY (Planning, Iter 1): Network scan complete — NO critical alerts, NO URGENT/DEFICIT requests, no shortages (<2), no hospital imbalances. Both hospitals fully cover queued Triage patients (8 IV_Kits + 8 PPE_Sets each) plus declared buffers. Therefore I am executing ZERO transfers this iteration: every unit pushed to a hospital without confirmed need = -10 holding cost, and there is no needy destination for a +15 transfer reward. DEEP RESERVES ON STANDBY for immediate dispatch on confirmed deficit: IV_Kits 70, PPE_Sets 77, Pain_Killers 37, Oxygen_Tanks 30, Radio_Contrast 24, Anesthetics 17, Surgical_Packs 17. PROTOCOL: (1) Request only NET-of-reservation deficits (net out Triage/Radiology/Surgery reservations first — avoid the GH double-count error); flag 'DEFICIT: <hospital> <resource> <amount>' and it moves immediately — emergency top-ups to prevent -300 failures are my top priority. (2) Surplus offers currently on the board (Pain_Killers ~8 per hospital, Radio_Contrast ~4 per hospital) should WAIT for a confirmed request from a needy hospital — +15/unit applies only to transfers into needy destinations; pushing surplus to a non-needy hospital nets negative. (3) If buffers go unused late in the episode, route true surplus to the other hospital on confirmed need (+15) rather than letting it sit (-10). I will re-scan every iteration and act on the first confirmed deficit.
Resource_Provisioner.rationale: Planning phase with zero alerts/deficits: any Provisioner→hospital send would be pure waste (-10/unit unused) and no needy destination exists for a +15 rewarded transfer. Broadcasting standby reserves + request protocol prevents double-commitment/over-buffering by departments, keeps central stock as free insurance against -300 failures, and primes hospitals to route surplus only to confirmed needy destinations for +15/unit. Will re-scan each iteration and dispatch instantly on any confirmed deficit.
